title: Sustainable Self-Development
description: Applications, definitions, key concepts, measures, and theories of sustainable development of individuals and society. Establishment of effective and potentially fulfilling sustainability lifestyle plan for the future. Interrelationships between biodiversity and society.

title: Wellness and Recreation for Life Through Surfing
description: This course explores links between recreation, society, and wellness through surfing culture and lifestyle. Surfing as a context for exploring human behavior, cognition, and organization.

title: Surfing and Science
description: Natural science exploration of surf related topics to include high quality surfing waves in the ocean and in human made surf lagoons, surfboard evolution from hand carved lumber to recycled ocean plastics, and, climate change resilience and surf ecosystem conservation.

title: Recreation, Travel, and Self-Awareness
description: How recreation and travel are influenced by economic, environmental, political, and socio-cultural forces. Impacts of recreation and travel on well-being and self-awareness.

title: Supervised Field Work
description: Observation and participation in community recreation leadership. Practical experience in a variety of recreational settings. Eight hours per week at an agency.

title: Data Driven Decision Making in Hospitality, Recreation, and Tourism
description: Quantitative and qualitative methods in hospitality, recreation, and tourism fields. Gathering data from sources, summarizing data points, analyses, reporting findings/results, conclusions and recommendations.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Service Leadership Development
description: Communication, creativity, group dynamics and leadership, problem solving, program planning, and publicity in recreation and tourism contexts.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Leisure and Tourism
description: Study of leisure and its impact on contemporary life; issues affecting recreation in today’s urbanized society.

title: Wilderness and the Leisure Experience
description: Values of protected landscapes to individuals and society. Scientific, political, international, and ethical dimensions of natural landscapes. Implications for protection, visitor management, and sustainable tourism.

title: Conduct of Recreational Sports
description: Organization of competition, community sports programs, administration of intramural athletics, and techniques of officiating.

title: Recreation Therapy and Special Populations
description: Sociopsychological aspects of special populations and their implications for leisure pursuits. Field trips may be included.

title: Recreation and Tourism Management
description: Through experiential learning incorporating local organizations, students gain real-world experience in, recreation and tourism management to include: needs assessment and services development; marketing; budget development; revenue generation; assets management; risk management; strategic planning; operation of facilities/areas; and, human resources.

title: Cross-Cultural Perspectives of Tourism
description: Concepts, definitions, and measures of essential cultural components of tourism. Integrated view of interrelated socio-cultural tourism issues with an understanding and appreciation of diverse cultures.

title: Cultural Tourism
description: Concepts of cultural tourism and cultural heritage management. Strategies for planning of cultural tourism resources and for development of cultural tourism initiatives. Evaluating tourism potential of cultural or heritage assets.

title: Marketing, Financing, and Assessment in Recreation and Tourism Management
description: Marketing, financing, and assessment specifically related to recreation and tourism management to include services development, pricing, promotion, distribution; budget development, revenue generation, assets management, controls; evaluation and research process as they relate to service development and delivery.

title: Administration and Operation of Recreation and Tourism Agencies
description: Administrative and operational aspects of managing and leading in recreation and tourism agencies to include liability, risk management, administrative regulations; information/decision systems in organizations; strategic planning; operation of facilities/areas; human resource functions related to successful service delivery.

title: Global Sustainable Tourism Management
description: Global tourism management, economics, development and sustainability. Social, cultural, and environmental impact indicators and management tools for sustainable development.

title: Commercial Recreation and Attractions Management
description: Analysis of commercial recreation field, including design, development, programming and marketing aspects of various commercial recreation enterprises.

title: Sustainable Tourism Planning
description: Nature and scope of sustainable tourism planning. Approaches, principles, and processes for creating sustainability value in tourism. Sustainability assessment and corporate social responsibility for tourism amenities, attractions, services, transportation and facilities.

title: Directed Leadership
description: Supervised leadership experience in public and private recreation agencies.

title: Outdoor Recreation Planning and Policy
description: Nature and scope of recreation in nonurban areas. Public demand for recreation and its impact on natural resources. Management, planning, research and operation of regional and national park and recreation areas.

title: Environmental and Cultural Interpretation
description: Philosophy, theory, methods, application, and scope of cultural interpretation in recreation and tourism settings.

title: Outdoor Leadership and Adventure Programming
description: Theoretical principles and experience in leadership, judgment, and decision making in outdoor adventure programming.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Internship in Recreation and Tourism Management
description: For six unit internship: 250 hours of professional work experience in recreation and tourism management.
notes: For 12 unit internship: 500 hours required Credit for course requires completion of ePortfolio.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Writing in Recreation Settings
description: Theory and practice of writing in the field of recreation and parks with application to various settings.
